author: mryzhov
title: smoke_ConvertCPULayerTest - primType is unexpected : unknown_f32 Expected : acl_f32 on ARM64
signature: primtype is unexpected unknown f32 expected acl f32|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: CPU functional tests / CPU functional tests
failed_jobs.symptom: smoke_ConvertCPULayerTest_4D_Dynamic assertion failure: primType unexpectedly unknown_f32 instead of acl_f32, process exits 255

key_errors:
src/plugins/intel_cpu/tests/functional/utils/cpu_test_utils.cpp:248: Failure
Value of: primTypeCheck(primType)
  Actual: false
Expected: true
primType is unexpected : unknown_f32 Expected : acl_f32
root_cause: On the ARM64 (ACL) execution path, ConvertCPULayerTest intermittently selects a generic 'unknown' primitive implementation instead of the expected 'acl' primitive for certain dynamic input-shape/precision combinations (f32->i32). This is a known recurring flaky-test signature on ARM64 cross-compilation runs (prior occurrence on 2026-07-20, PR #36885, plus closely related primType-mismatch variants against other precisions seen repeatedly since July). The test assertion is overly strict about which primitive implementation ACL dispatches to at runtime, and that dispatch can vary under certain parallel-test-runner scheduling/resource conditions on the ARM64 runner, producing an assertion failure rather than a real correctness bug. The failing job was on its first attempt and a second automatic re-run attempt (run_attempt 2) of the same job subsequently succeeded, consistent with a transient/flaky primitive-selection issue rather than a deterministic code defect introduced by PR #39101 (whose changes are confined to CI wheel-build/workflow files and LLM test requirements, unrelated to CPU ACL primitive dispatch).
reproduction_steps: Run the CPU functional test suite with gtest_filter='*smoke_ConvertCPULayerTest_4D_Dynamic*' on an ARM64 build with the ACL backend enabled; the failure is intermittent and may require several repeated runs to reproduce locally.
recommended_actions: Investigate why ACL sometimes reports/dispatches an 'unknown' primitive type instead of 'acl' for ConvertCPULayerTest on ARM64, focusing on src/plugins/intel_cpu/tests/functional/utils/cpu_test_utils.cpp:248 and the ACL executor selection logic in src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes for Convert.
Consider relaxing or correctly asserting primType expectations for dynamic-shape Convert cases if 'unknown' is a legitimate fallback for some shapes rather than a bug.

Re-run the failed job (already succeeded on attempt 2) and monitor for recurrence; if it keeps recurring, approve the proposed rerun pattern so the automated rerunner can retry it without manual intervention.
prevention_strategies: Track flaky ARM64/ACL primType-mismatch tests in a quarantine/known-flaky list so merge-queue runs are not blocked by them, and route PRs touching CPU plugin ACL executor-selection code through additional ARM64 regression runs before merge.
historical_context: Multiple near-identical primType-mismatch signatures have recurred on ARM64 since July 2026 across different precision pairs (f32/i32/i8) and categorizations (some filed as Code Issue, some as Flaky Test), e.g. patterns 0de8f57e3fb03230 (this exact f32->acl_f32 signature, first seen 2026-07-20, PR #36885), 67be3af52d03d193, 76751669c7a78fcd, cb7d14bccc236de4, a5dbac5de6377592, 8664b9fc6e97654f, f7a6dd5a16071269, and the related MaxPool ARM64 primType pattern eb0b94c864ee1a85 (8 occurrences). None have a committed fix yet; this investigation reinforces classification as Flaky Test given the job succeeded on automatic retry.
